sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640, along with one Raghu as pillion rider, near Srinivasa Nursery,
Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City.

At that time, the driver of the auto-ricksaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 came from opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the petitioner was shifted to Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Tavarekere Police have registered the case against the driver of the said auto for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of "Digit commercial vehicle package policy - passenger carrying vehicle" policy in respect of auto bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762 in favour of respondent No.1 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 150(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has further contended that, the alleged accident has caused due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
There is delay in lodging the complaint with respect of alleged accident.
No valid reasons are assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.

The petitioner in order to claim compensation has falsely implicated the auto-rickshaw Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
2 bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762, in collusion with the insured and the police.
The driver of the offending auto-rickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

As such the jurisdictional police have filed charge- sheet under Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act stating that, the driver of the auto-rickshaw was not holding driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident.
It has further contended that, the auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in the place of accident and it is violation of the policy conditions.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has denied the occurrence and mode of accident and also involvement of the auto-rickshaw.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident, alleged to have occurred on 06-07-2022 at about 12:15 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto Rickshaw bearing registration No. KA-03-AC-9762 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Arjun S.
Prakash as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondents No.2 has examined its official as R.W.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed its side.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.
8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., when he was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640, along with one Raghu as pillion rider, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, the driver of the auto- ricksaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 came from opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner, without Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
3 observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition and got marked total 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is discharge summary, Ex.P.8 is notarised copy of Aadhar card,
Ex.P.9 are medical bills (total 46), Ex.P.10 are prescriptions (total 28) and Ex.P.11 are x-rays (total 2).

11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, on 06-07- 2022 at about 12.15 p.m., when he was riding his motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640, along with one Raghu as pillion rider, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli,
Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, the driver of the auto- ricksaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 came from opposite direction, in a rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner and pillion rider fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report, which is marked as Ex.P.3, has clearly stated that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, the date, time and place of accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 with respect to auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company, though has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident is caused due to self negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle i.e. petitioner and the auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762 has been falsely implicated in the case by the petitioner, has not produced any evidence to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is no other rebuttal oral or documentary evidence produced by the respondent No.1 to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Further, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident has caused due to his self negligence and he have lodged false complaint against the driver of auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
4 said accident has caused due to negligent riding on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 and there is no negligence driving on the part of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-03-AC-9762.

13. The Ex.P.4 spot mahazer clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 22 feet wide Ramohalli- Doddaladamara road, near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, in between motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640 and car bearing No.KA-03-AC- 9762.

Further, the damage caused to both the vehicles on the front portion, as noted in the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident report, clearly goes to show that, the said accident is caused due to head collusion of both the vehicles.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.3 final report has clearly stated that, the alleged accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762.
14.
Further, as per the Ex.P.5 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC- 9762.

When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-41-W-5640, then in the present facts and circumstances, it can be presumed that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762.
Further, admittedly the final report/charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged by the driver or by the owner of offending auto-rickshaw bearing No. KA-03-AC-9762.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary and Ex.P.11 X- rays, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left.
The same has been deposed by the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner and assessed the disability to the petitioner.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents No.2 to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false created documents.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 insurance company has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto- rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
Further, there is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: 18. Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 06-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., near Srinivasa Nursery, Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA- 03-AC-9762.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-03-AC-9762 and he has sustained acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants,
transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
As per Ex.P.8, the year of birth of the petitioner is 1984.
The accident has taken place on 06-07- 2022 at about 12:15 p.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 38 years.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability to the petitioner, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 54.47% physical disability of limbs and 18.15%
physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.6 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary and Ex.P.11 X- rays clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 06-07-2022 and he has assessed the Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
6 disability to the petitioner on 14-01-2024, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, he has deposed that, the fractures sustained by the petitioner are united.
Further, he has deposed that, the petitioner is required to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, the P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, the fractures sustained by the petitioner are united and there is no loss of muscles and weakness to the petitioner.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and the oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as painter and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as painter.
In such circumstances, there is no other option except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident had taken place in 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 38 years is 15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 10/100 X 15 = Rs.2,79,000/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.4,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 46 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the bills at serial No.2, 4 and 11 are not in the name of the petitioner.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.

Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.3,78,465/- towards medical expenses and she is entitled for the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:
In the present case, the evidence on record clearly establishes that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. suffered acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left.
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 13 days from 06-07-2022 to 18-07-2023,78,4652, in Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.

In such circumstances, certainly the Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
7 petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
iv) Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 13 days from 06-07-2022 to 18-07-2022, in Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.1000 x 13 = Rs.13,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.7 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 13 days from 06-07-2022 to 18-07-2022, in Shreya Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore,
compensation of Rs.800 x 13 = Rs.10,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of K. Rampura, Chunchanakuppe, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru, the accident has taken place in front of crimes on near Srinivasa Nursery,
Ketohalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru City and he has taken treatment at Shreya Hospital,
Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between all the above three places

,
compensation of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 13 days as inpatient at Shreya Hospital Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.15,500 x 2 =
Rs.31,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 38 years and unfortunately he has suffered acute SDH and fracture of acetabulam left.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has stated in his chief-examination that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost Rs.70,000/-.
But, he has not provided any estimation with respect to said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows :
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,79,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 3,78,465-00 3.
Pain and sufferings 40,000-00

Conveyance expenses 2,000-00 7. Loss of income during 31,000-00 treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 20,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00 Total Rs. 7,93,865-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,93,865/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
Now the question before this Court is, who is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 the accident has occurred.

In such circumstances,
the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
22.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the Ex.R.1 Insurance Policy clearly speaks that, the policy covers the risk provided the driver of offending vehicle holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.

The Ex.P.3 charge-sheet clearly speaks that, as on the date of accident the accused/driver of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C., he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Admittedly, the final report filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged either by the driver of by the owner offending auto-rickshaw.
Even, the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending auto- rickshaw was holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle, who has consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence to drive the said vehicle, cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

In support of his arguments, he has relied on the following decisions:
i) Beli Ram V/s Rajinder Kumar and another, reported in AIR 2020 SC 4453.

sentences.text: Admittedly, in the instant case, as on the date of alleged accident the driver of the offending auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-03-AC-9762 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, before handing over the offending vehicle to his driver/accused, the respondent No.1 was not aware or he was not conscious that his driver was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Further, it is pertinent to note the, even after issuance of notice by the respondent No.2 issurance company U/Sec.134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act, to the accused/driver of offending auto-rickshaw and also to his father, to produce the driving licence of the driver of offending auto-rickshaw namely Mahadev N S/o Narayanappa, they have failed to produce the same.
In such circumstances, it leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the said driver and hold that, he was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Even, there is no document produced in the case to show that, the offending vehicle was having valid permit as on the date of accident, to ply the said vehicle in the place of accident.

In such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner does not hold good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, relied by him, is not applicable to the case in hand.

On the other hand, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 hold good and the ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, relied by him, is aptly applicable to the case in hand.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court comes to conclusion that, the respondent No.1 being the owner of offending vehicle is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

As there is fundamental Kumar R.C vs Nayazkhan on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177072545/
10 breach of insurance policy conditions by the respondent No.1, the respondent No.2 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Further, as the cause of action for filing the present claim petition has arose after coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019,
the pay and recovery principle is not applicable to the case in hand.

Accordingly, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,93,865/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization
, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
25. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.7,93,865/- (Rupees seven lakh ninety three thousand eight hundred and sixty five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
(excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
The petition against respondent No.2 is dismissed.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
